bullets.title: NVDA earnings tonight: buyside expects $94-95B rev beat, $107-110B guide; options price ~5.4% move
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side desks (JPM, UBS, GS) coalesce around buyside consensus of ~$94-95B Q2 revenue (a ~$2B sequential beat vs. Street at $92B) with October-quarter guidance of $107-108B; some buyside models discuss $110B+. Options market implies only ~5.4% move—lowest in 8 quarters—reflecting massive market-cap SPX weighting. Key investor focus: capex sustainability, AI infrastructure financing, competitive ASIC pressure (OpenAI Jalapeño), HBM de-spec scenarios, and China business outlook. NVDA has sold off after each of its last four earnings reports despite beats.

bullets.title: OpenAI Jalapeño chip reportedly outperforms NVDA Blackwell on perf/watt; AVGO is partner
bullets.body: Hot Chips 2026 reveal: OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC (co-developed with AVGO, co-manufactured by Broadcom) reportedly delivers 1.5-2x better throughput/watt vs. NVDA GB200/GB300 and 1.7-3.6x lower latency, operating at 700W vs. NVDA's 1,200-1,400W. Jalapeño pairs with 216GB HBM4 at 15.4 TB/s. If production scales through 2027, analysts see material risk to NVDA's CUDA moat and hyperscaler GPU reliance. UBS notes OpenAI chip claims as positive for AVGO specifically.

bullets.title: AI networking is the new compute bottleneck; NVDA, AVGO, ANET, MRVL, COHR, LITE benefit
bullets.body: Citi's Hot Chips Day 2 note argues data movement—not raw compute—is now the critical bottleneck in AI factories. NVDA's Spectrum-X Ethernet Multiplane architecture scales to 512k GPUs; AVGO's Thor Ultra, Arista, and co-packaged optics vendors (Lumentum, Coherent) are well-positioned. Memory innovations (LPDDR5X-PIM, CXL) are effectively specialized networking solutions. Google TPU v8 superpod will have 9,600 chips with 2PB shared memory, underscoring network-centric design trends.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure demand exceptionally strong; HBM tight into 2027, memory prices surging
bullets.body: JPM Asia Tech Tour finds GPU/ASIC demand exceptionally strong with intensifying bottlenecks in advanced packaging and substrates; TSMC's dominance reinforced. HBM remains in serious shortage expected into 2027; DDR5 16Gb spot prices rose +6% MoM (+880% YoY); NAND rebounded +14% MoM. Samsung and SK Hynix increasing 8-high HBM4 shipments, reshaping NVDA's supply chain. WFE buy-side forecasts tracking at or above bull-case assumptions of $155-165B for 2026.

bullets.title: INTU down ~9% premarket on FY27 reset: revenue guide +9-10% vs consensus +11%, TurboTax to +2-3%
bullets.body: Intuit's FQ4 beat (revenue +14% YoY, EPS $4.03 vs $3.58 est) was overshadowed by a deep FY27 reset: revenue guided to $23.28-23.51B (consensus $23.72B), TurboTax growth guided to +2-3% (vs +7% in FY26) as AI disruption hits low-end DIY filers. Three-year GBSG CAGR lowered to 10-15% from 15-20%. JPM downgrades to Neutral, cuts PT to $331 from $605; Piper downgrades to Underweight ($290 PT); NTM P/E compresses to ~13.6x vs. 5-year avg 31x. FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide $28.69-28.93 above consensus on workforce cuts and efficiency.

bullets.title: Broad SaaS weakness premarket; IGV -2.2% YTD vs S&P +12.9%; AI disruption scrutiny widening
bullets.body: INTU and ZM both declined post-earnings, with SaaS/cloud names broadly weak in premarket (NOW, SNOW, TEAM, HUBS, NET, DDOG all down 1.3-2.8%). Wolfe All-SaaS index at 5.7x FY+2 EV/Sales with multiples down 2.58% week-over-week. ZM's enterprise revenue accelerated to 7.8% YoY but online decelerated to 0.6% YoY; full-year FCF raised to $1.78-1.82B (35.4% margin).

bullets.title: Semtech (SMTC) blowout: Q3 data center guided +45% QoQ, +160% YoY; record backlog
bullets.body: Semtech reported Q2 EPS $0.71 vs $0.61 est; Q3 guidance $410-415M vs $360M consensus, with data center revenue guided +45% QoQ and +160% YoY in Q3 driven by FiberEdge 1.6T and CopperEdge. Record backlog provides >70% FY28 visibility. Gross margin improving to 58.3% in Q3 post cellular module divestiture. Data center expected to reach $200M+/quarter run rate by FQ1 2028.

bullets.title: Oil drops ~3-4% on Iran-Oman Strait of Hormuz framework talks; yields fall 7bp
bullets.body: Iran and Oman reached a preliminary framework to temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz via a toll-managed corridor and mine-clearing project; Rubio confirmed U.S. unlikely to launch new Iran strikes near-term. Brent settled at $88.58 (-3.9%), WTI at $82.36 (-3.1%). The de-escalation pushed 10-year Treasury yields down ~7bp to 4.63% and helped lift equities: S&P +0.34%, Nasdaq 100 +0.6%. Tanker traffic through Hormuz had dropped to only 5 vessels Tuesday vs. 15-vessel 10-day average.

bullets.title: Fed internally divided: 4 of 12 banks sought July rate hike; Barkin calls decision 'close call'
bullets.body: Fed minutes revealed four regional Fed bank directors voted to raise the discount rate at the July meeting, with the full FOMC voting 9-3 to hold. Richmond Fed's Barkin characterized the July hold as a 'close call' and flagged U.S. public debt surpassing $40T as a sustainability risk. Jackson Hole speech by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday is the next major policy catalyst; markets positioned for growth/size factor outperformance in the 1-3 weeks post-Jackson Hole.

bullets.title: ECB ready to hike 25bp in September; eurozone inflation near 3% driven by Iran energy shock
bullets.body: Multiple ECB policymakers signal readiness to raise rates in September to address Iran-war energy-driven inflation near 3%, but show little appetite for additional tightening signals beyond September. ECB's Schnabel described the economy as gaining momentum but cautioned on natural gas. ANZ Bank separately forecasts RBA hiking 25bp in November as Australian CPI came in at 3.5% YoY (est 3.3%) with trimmed mean at 3.6%.

bullets.title: US-Canada trade war escalates: 50% tariffs on $20B Canadian goods; Canada retaliates dollar-for-dollar
bullets.body: The Trump administration imposed 50% tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods (steel, aluminum, electronics); Canadian PM Carney announced matching dollar-for-dollar retaliation starting September 8. GS recommends buying USDCAD 1.40 calls (2-month, 4.8 vol/24.5bp) as CAD depreciation risk remains underpriced in options despite repeated escalation headlines.

bullets.title: Gold hits $4,657 (+8% in a week) on fiscal concerns, debasement trade, weaker dollar
bullets.body: Gold closed at $4,657/oz after four consecutive sessions of gains, driven by falling Treasury yields from Treasury buyback operations, a weaker USD, and growing U.S. fiscal stability concerns (national debt surpassed $40T at 123% of GDP). Citi targets $5,000 for gold over the next year; Jackson Hole speech seen as near-term catalyst—dovish = bullish for gold, hawkish = halt.

bullets.title: Alibaba: $10B HK placement signals CCP AI support; Jack Ma and co-founders buying $100M+
bullets.body: Alibaba's HK$80B follow-on placement (completed at 8.4% discount) was interpreted by Jefferies as signaling Communist Party backing for AI buildout. JP Morgan maintains OW, arguing compute IRR of 22% vs. ~10% cost of capital makes capex economics sound. Jack Ma purchased $76.5M of BABA; co-founders Joseph Tsai ($20.7M) and Eddie Wu ($4.98M) also bought in recent days. China AI capex forecast raised 23% over 5-year cumulative estimate.

bullets.title: META up ~1.3% premarket on settlement talks with state AGs over teen addiction trial
bullets.body: Meta is in settlement discussions with 29 state attorneys general during the second week of an 8-10 week trial alleging Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict teenagers. Meta models worst-case judgment near $1.4T (near its market cap); any settlement would likely be far less and is being characterized by investors as a potential non-recurring one-time event. CEO Zuckerberg expected to testify.

bullets.title: Healthcare sector surges: XLV hit all-time high, +7.8% in August; GS Most Short HC basket +5.2% Tuesday
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Quad 1 'Dollylocks' framework (declining inflation rate-of-change + accelerating real growth) is bullish on healthcare: XLV and FXH are their #1 US equity sector allocation. 468 of S&P 500 companies posted +50% YoY EPS acceleration. HYG high yield hit all-time high. Oil's break below key levels opened further selling, lowering UST 10Y TRADE Signal to 4.67%.

bullets.title: DKS down ~31% post-earnings: Foot Locker comps -3.6% drag; 3 downgrades, NKE also cut
bullets.body: Dick's Sporting Goods missed Q2 by 0.9% revenue and 6.1% EPS, with core DKS comps +4.9% but Foot Locker comps -3.6% dragging results. FL guided to a segment loss of ($80M-$40M) vs. prior profit of $110-150M. Three downgrades (Telsey to $145, Truist to $135, KGI to neutral) and NTM P/E of 8.5x vs. 5-year average of 12.0x. GS argues the weakness is FL-specific (inventory excess, footwear softness) not competitive; DKS core business maintained 4.9% comp growth. Truist also downgraded NKE to Hold ($42 PT).

bullets.title: Treasury long-end buyback underperforms: accepted only $1.19B of $8.4B offered; curve implications
bullets.body: Treasury's buyback of 2031-2033 coupons accepted just $1.19B (14.2% hit rate) vs. the $4B forecast, covering only 10 of 25 eligible issues. JPM notes increased buyback frequency has smoothed price impacts but GS argues long-end buybacks are unlikely to address the macro drivers of higher long-term yields. The 5s/30s curve at 78-81bp support is a key technical level; inability to hold would derail medium-term steepening momentum.

bullets.title: Moonshot AI (China) in early talks with MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL to host Kimi K3 at up to 30% revenue share
bullets.body: Reuters reports Moonshot AI is negotiating a potential first-of-its-kind revenue-sharing deal with Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, and Google Cloud to host its Kimi K3 model; Moonshot would seek up to 30% of related cloud service revenue. Talks are early-stage. Separately, China's DeepSeek revenue hit $70.7M in Jan-Jul 2026 (~10x full-year 2025) and is seeking a second funding round at RMB 500B valuation.

bullets.title: ORCL added to Citi upside catalyst watch; CDS at record wides create opportunity per Citi
bullets.body: Citi opened a positive 90-day catalyst watch on ORCL after a 30%+ drawdown (50%+ peak-to-trough, 4-5 standard deviation move) and noted ORCL added $85B+ QoQ backlog in May 2026. CDS spreads reportedly exceeded 2008 crisis peaks (per Twitter), which Citi interprets as investor capitulation creating entry opportunity. FY30 EPS estimated at $22, 18x PT = $330. Q1 earnings (~Sep 10) and October AI World investor day are key catalysts.

bullets.title: Copper hits all-time high; data center gas demand upgraded to 10-11 bcf/d by 2030; pipeline stocks favored
bullets.body: Copper reached a record closing price during the session. GS raised its data center-driven natural gas demand forecast to 10-11 bcf/d by 2030 (from 7-8 bcf/d), rating WMB and KMI Buy as preferred pipeline beneficiaries. Large-scale pipeline and power project announcements expected in 2H26 as catalysts for energy equities.
